tier_rationale: Sold in the manufacturer's explicitly non-cellular line with images written directly to SD card, and the grantee that files Browning's trail-camera authorizations holds a cellular grant only for the Command X model — no radio grant exists for the non-cellular cameras.
the_unplug_test: Irrelevant, and that is the point. This camera never had a connection to lose. It writes to an SD card you physically walk out and collect. There is no subscription, no data plan, no account, and no company that can decide your camera stops uploading. Because there is no cellular radio drawing power, a set of AA batteries lasts six to twelve months instead of weeks.

repairability.notes: Standard AA batteries and a removable SD card are the only consumables — no sealed battery pack to age out.

sources.supports: Manufacturer's non-cellular collection lists this model at $139.99 and describes the line as no-subscription, writing image and video directly to SD card. Cellular models are segregated into a separate collection with mobile service plans.

Sibling control: Quest Cameras LLC (grantee 2BGC), which files Browning's trail-camera authorizations, holds 2BGCQCOMMANDX covering LTE cellular for the Command X. No radio grant exists for the non-cellular Strike Force or Command Ops models, ruling out Bluetooth setup radios as well as cellular.

open_questions: Confirm from the printed manual that firmware updates are SD-card only on this model.
notes: Trail cameras are one of the few categories where the dumb option is also the better-performing one: no cellular radio means battery life measured in months rather than weeks, and no monthly bill. The whole category splits cleanly on this line, which makes it unusually easy to shop.
